left.heading: WHAT IT IS:
left.body: Under 4,000 lines of kernel code doing one job with one set of ciphers.
left.draw: A dark code editor window showing `static int wg_xmit(....) {`, a Linux penguin standing beside it, and a small shield badge reading `<4000 LINES`.

right.heading: WHY IT WON:
right.body: Small enough to audit end to end, and fast enough that nobody argues about it.
right.draw: A clipboard headed `AUDIT` with three ticked checkboxes, next to a stopwatch drawn with motion lines behind it.

how.heading: HOW IT WORKS
how.subtitle: Four design decisions that define the protocol.

cards.heading: PUBLIC KEYS ONLY
cards.body: Each peer is identified by a single 32-byte public key. No certificates, no usernames, no PKI to run.
cards.draw: A key joined to a short pipe with an arrow pointing to a second key, above a paper certificate with a wax seal struck through by a large red cross.

cards.heading: CRYPTOKEY ROUTING
cards.body: Each key is bound to a list of allowed IPs. That one table decides who may send what, and where it goes.
cards.draw: A two-column table headed `PUBLIC KEY` and `ALLOWED IPS` with four rows of key glyphs and CIDR ranges, one row highlighted, an arrow leaving it toward a network port.

cards.heading: ONE FIXED SUITE
cards.body: ChaCha20 with Poly1305, Curve25519, BLAKE2s. Nothing is negotiated, so there is nothing to downgrade.
cards.draw: A closed box labelled `ONE SUITE` with a green tick beside it, next to a folded menu card listing `AES-GCM`, `AES-CBC`, `DES`, `3DES`, `RC4` all struck through in red.

cards.heading: SILENT BY DEFAULT
cards.body: It never replies to an unauthenticated packet. To a port scanner the service looks like it is not there.
cards.draw: A dark server rack with a large magnifying glass held over it showing only three dots inside, and an empty speech bubble containing three dots.

costs.heading: WHAT IT COSTS YOU
costs.subtitle: The trade-offs that come with being this small.

cards.heading: UDP ONLY
cards.body: There is no TCP fallback. If the network blocks UDP, you are simply not connecting.
cards.draw: A wide pipe labelled `UDP` slamming into a brick wall and shattering at the point of contact.

cards.heading: THE PEER MAPPING
cards.body: The server keeps the key-to-IP table. On somebody else's server that is a persistent identifier for you.
cards.draw: An open ledger book with columns `PUBLIC KEY` and `LAST SEEN IP`, four rows, one highlighted, and a large eye watching from above a server rack.

cards.heading: KEY MANAGEMENT IS YOURS
cards.body: No usernames, no per-user credentials, no simple revocation once you have many peers.
cards.draw: An open upturned hand with four keys floating above it and a question mark hanging among them.

cards.heading: ALL ENDPOINTS UPDATE TOGETHER
cards.body: No cipher agility means if a primitive ever breaks, everything must be upgraded at once.
cards.draw: A clock at the top connected by branching lines to four devices in a row, each with an upward arrow beneath it.
